name: Midian
overview: Midian is a male figure in Scripture, uniquely identified as a son of Abraham through his wife Keturah. The Bible records him as one of the descendants Abraham fathered after Sarah's death, highlighting his role in the continuation of Abraham's lineage. No further tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided about Midian.
namesAndTitles: The name Midian means 'quarrel, strife, contention,' reflecting a possible characteristic or circumstance associated with his lineage. This proper name was not given directly by God but is recorded in Genesis 25:2.
familyAndRelationships: Midian is recorded as a son of Abraham and Keturah. He is also noted as the father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. Additionally, the figure Zur is connected as an ancestor in his line, indicating a continuing family legacy mentioned in Numbers 25:15.
scriptureSignificance: Midian's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a progenitor of a distinct lineage stemming from Abraham after the covenantal line through Isaac. His descendants, known as the Midianites, appear later in Scripture, marking his importance in the broader story of God's dealings with Abraham's offspring. Through Midian, the Scriptures demonstrate God's providential unfolding of nations originating from Abraham, underscoring the faithfulness of God's promises.
